title: A money type with standard traits
description:
Give a type the standard traits so it works with operators, printing and sorting.

```
£12.50 + £3.75 = £16.25
£12.50 > £3.75: true
sorted: [£0.99, £3.75, £12.50]
default: £0.00
```
hints: `impl fmt::Display for Money { fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result { write!(f, "£{}.{:02}", ...) } }` (lesson 4.03).
`impl From<f64> for Money { fn from(x: f64) -> Self { Money { pence: (x * 100.0).round() as i64 } } }` lets you write `Money::from(3.75)` and `let m: Money = 3.75.into();`.
requirements: `struct Money { pence: i64 }` with `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Default)]`.
